videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum

verb, second conjugation, transitive

The everyday word for seeing with the eyes, and also for seeing to something (vidē ut) and for understanding (see I get it). The passive videor is “seem” (see seem).

Other words

  • cernō, cernere, crēvī, crētum — make out, see clearly

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. videō: syn. cernō

    Seeing something distinctly, picking it out from what is around it; its perfect crēvī sounds like the perfect of crēscō, so in speech prefer vīdī.

  • cōnspiciō, cōnspicere, cōnspexī, cōnspectum — catch sight of

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Ter., Cic., Caes. (Lewis & Short); Traupman 287; Traupman 379

    Getting a sight of someone or something, often suddenly: “there he is!”

Examples

  • phasēlus ille, quem vidētis, hospitēs, ait fuisse nāvium celerrimus

    that boat you see, my guests, claims she was once the fastest of shipsCatull. 4.1–2

  • Oculus videt colōrēs, quid album vel ātrum, viride vel caeruleum, rubrum aut lūteum sit.

    The eye sees colours, what is white or black, green or blue, red or yellow.Comen. OP 41

  • Vidēsne illam nāvem? — Videō.

    Can you see that ship? — Yes.composed

  • revidēre

    to see againTraupman 376

See also notice, eye, seem, appear, I get it!, meet.
